title: Orientation I: What the Way Is
purpose: Give participants a complete map of the Way without asking them to join, agree, donate, or disclose private beliefs.
dissent_prompt: What is one feature of this project you currently distrust, dislike, or think could fail?
between_session_practice: During the week, notice one moment when you encounter a question of meaning, truth, suffering, beauty, duty, or transcendence. Write what happened before deciding what it “means.”
custom_feedback: After Week 1, I can explain at least two differences between the Assembly and the future corporation.

title: Orientation II: How We Know
purpose: Teach the Way’s core discipline for distinguishing experience, report, interpretation, institutional teaching, and confidence.
dissent_prompt: Where could this evidence-and-confidence system itself become a source of false certainty or bias?
between_session_practice: Choose one strong belief you hold—religious or nonreligious. Write: What is the claim? What kind of claim is it? What supports it? What would make you revise it?
custom_feedback: I can distinguish a testimony from the interpretation attached to it.

title: Prayer I: Attention and Honest Address
purpose: Pilot prayer that permits belief, doubt, silence, lament, gratitude, petition, and nonparticipation without emotional pressure.
dissent_prompt: What forms of prayer or language about God would make participation difficult for you?
between_session_practice: Try 5-10 minutes on three days: stillness, gratitude/lament, and dedication. Record only what you observed—not what you think you “should” have experienced.
custom_feedback: I felt free to participate, observe, modify, or decline the prayer practices.

title: Study I: Reading Witnesses Responsibly
purpose: Practice reading sacred and historical witnesses without confusing reverence, source proximity, genre, and truth claims.
dissent_prompt: When does critical study feel illuminating, and when does it feel reductive or unfair?
between_session_practice: Choose one religious story you know. Identify its source, genre, approximate date/setting if known, and one question the source can answer versus one it cannot answer by itself.
custom_feedback: I can explain the difference between a text being spiritually important and a text being early historical evidence.

title: Fellowship: The Common Table
purpose: Test whether shared food and conversation can embody companionship, equality, hospitality, and ordinary friendship without insider hierarchy.
dissent_prompt: What could make a shared religious meal feel manipulative, exclusionary, or status-conscious?
between_session_practice: Offer one act of hospitality this week that creates no debt and no expectation of religious agreement.
custom_feedback: The fellowship period felt status-neutral rather than leader-centered or insider-centered.

title: Service: Good Without Conversion
purpose: Make outward service a constitutive practice while preventing aid from becoming a recruitment or loyalty tool.
dissent_prompt: What harms can occur when religious communities combine service with recruitment or publicity?
between_session_practice: Complete one modest service act or planning step. Record what the recipient/community actually needed versus what you initially assumed.
custom_feedback: I understood that aid or service from this community is not conditioned on religious participation.

title: Discernment I: Disagreement Without Defeat
purpose: Practice a decision process that can hear disagreement, preserve minority concerns, and reach a bounded decision without treating dissent as disloyalty.
dissent_prompt: If you disagreed with the outcome, were your reasons represented accurately and without penalty?
between_session_practice: Notice one decision this week where you can separate: facts, values, preferences, risks, and uncertainty.
custom_feedback: I could disagree with the proposed decision without feeling I was opposing the community itself.

title: Ethics, Power, and Boundaries
purpose: Teach the difference between spiritual care and coercive control through concrete scenarios involving money, sex, confidentiality, housing, health, and authority.
dissent_prompt: Which power relationship worries you most in religious organizations, and what control would you require?
between_session_practice: Write three sentences you could use to maintain a boundary with a respected spiritual leader.
custom_feedback: I can identify when a “spiritual” issue should instead trigger ordinary safeguarding, legal, medical, or financial processes.

title: Open Theology: What We Do Not Yet Know
purpose: Normalize disciplined uncertainty and allow participants to engage major theological questions without being pushed toward a founder-preferred answer.
dissent_prompt: Which major theological question do you think the Assembly should resolve sooner—and which should it resist resolving?
between_session_practice: Write one paragraph using all four stems: what you think, what you hope, what you do not know, and what evidence would matter.
custom_feedback: The facilitator distinguished uncertainty from indifference and did not pressure a theological conclusion.

title: Companion Pathway
purpose: Let participants examine Companion identity carefully without an altar-call dynamic, countdown, social pressure, or hidden legal consequences.
dissent_prompt: What would make “Companion” identity feel like social pressure or an insider/outsider caste?
between_session_practice: Do nothing for at least 48 hours except reflect. If you are considering Companion identity, write both your reasons for and reasons against it.
custom_feedback: I felt equally free to become a Companion, wait, remain a participant, or leave.

title: Founder-Exit Exercise
purpose: Test whether a gathering can function from written systems when the founder is absent and whether participants know what to do when founder preferences are unavailable.
dissent_prompt: What part of the community still feels too dependent on the founder?
between_session_practice: None required. Facilitator and founder convert findings into concrete remediation tasks.
custom_feedback: The gathering functioned without needing the founder’s permission, interpretation, or presence.

title: Repair, Complaints, and Leaving Well
purpose: Rehearse the systems that matter most when something goes wrong: complaint, independent review, non-retaliation, correction, departure, and repair.
dissent_prompt: What would make you distrust the complaint or exit system in practice?
between_session_practice: Keep the concern-route card somewhere accessible. No personal disclosure assignment.
custom_feedback: I know how to raise a concern outside the founder/facilitator chain if necessary.

title: Day-90 Review and Closure Decision
purpose: Decide from evidence—not momentum—whether the pilot should continue, revise and repeat, pause, close, or later seek House-in-Formation status after incorporation.
dissent_prompt: What is the strongest argument *against* continuing the pilot in its current form?
between_session_practice: No homework. Participants receive the final pilot summary and may disengage without follow-up pressure.
custom_feedback: The Day-90 decision reflected evidence and dissent rather than momentum or founder preference.
